# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-20

**The Indonesia long-form's first subscribers are in: 3.2 per 1,000 views against 2 for the Asia long-form, on 60,467 views in 69 hours, so the Bali follow-up stays. The Tipu Short is due today with no script on disk; it lapses on 23 November.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Due today, the calendar's date for him, and still no script on disk. It is the owner's pick of 15 November: the prize money and palace treasure taken on 4 May 1799, then the British writing of Tipu as a tyrant. Correction to yesterday: he is back in the news, a Tipu Jayanti row in News18 Marathi on 19 November.  
   First step: Script and record today. Open on the British verdict on him, then who wrote it after splitting his treasure, with one sum from the prize records, checked. “Tipu Sultan” first in the title. Ship by 22 November.
2. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: The top date on the radar, four days out, and it sits with Aurangzeb, the subject of the channel's two largest videos. Videos that size brought 65.9% of lifetime subscribers; this month 0 against 1,378 planned. It rests on the date and the name: Mughal Shorts with no film behind them have landed at or below the usual.  
   First step: Script on disk by 21 November: sentence one is Aurangzeb's order, the place and the date, an act of state, not a martyrdom story. Title starts “Guru Tegh Bahadur”. Record on 22, publish the evening of 23.
3. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form has 60,467 views in 69 hours, and its first day of subscribers is in: 3.2 per 1,000 views against 2 for the Asia long-form. A video still climbing is the moment to give its viewers the next one. The topic is a guess from its comments, from Java and Indonesia.  
   First step: After the two dated Shorts, list sources on Majapahit's fall and who moved to Bali. On 22 November, with three days of data, drop this if the Indonesia rate falls below the Asia long-form's.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,000 subscribers against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 19,587, which needs 63.9 net a day; the 7-day rate is 90.4 and the 28-day rate 44.7. Projection basis: 28-day rate; the 7-day rate is a spike. On that basis the month ends at 18,447, 1,140 short, and the channel is 900 behind the ramp today. Only 43.6% of net subscribers over 28 days came from videos; the rest is tied to no video and can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts, 0 against 1,378 this month; one video of that size closes it. Last week five Shorts shipped and none came from this list; the first two Ravana film Shorts beat the usual and the two Rama Shorts after them fell below it, so this week's Shorts are dated moments, not the film. Today's Short on Sonia Gandhi and Narasimha Rao was not on the list either; Shorts on recent politics have landed below the usual here, so judge it on 23 November before making another.

What's working
- “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana” runs at 875.5 views an hour; the Asia long-form has averaged 310.5 over its life. Its like rate is 1.8% against 0.9%, and on launch day it converted better too. Today is its day three.
- Long-form still brings most of what uploads bring: 74.9% of upload-attributed net subscribers over 28 days, on 40.7% of upload views.
- The best converter in the 90-day window is “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.1 net subscribers per 1,000 views. Its lesson is the Tipu Short's shape: “Name the villain, convict him with a document or payment he cannot deny, then end on who is still repeating him today.”

What's wrong
- Neither dated Short has a script on disk, and Tipu is due today. Probable cause: the owner's own picks take the week (Sonia Gandhi today; the Malay Ramayana, Thailand and Param Vir Chakra Shorts written since 19 November). Test: none. If only one dated Short can be made before 24 November, make Tegh Bahadur and drop Tipu on the Today tab so the list stays honest.
- Film reach is not turning into subscribers: the Indonesia long-form 3.2 per 1,000 views, the Asia long-form 2, “Why Ravana Kidnapped Sita” 0.2. Long-form over the 365-day window has fallen out of its usual range to 8, and only 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged views. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing, and videos that tour a story without convicting anyone. Test: the Indonesia video names who rewrote the story; compare its rate with the Asia one's on 22 November.
- Long-form views fell 33.7% and watch time 38.3% week over week to 2026-11-17. Probable cause: the Asia long-form's Home-feed run ended, and the Indonesia launch has one day in the window (22,710 long-form views that day). Test: the week to 24 November.
- The Ramayana film has stopped paying on Shorts: “Every Ramayana Kept One Rule” has 1,669 views and “Why Is Lord Rama in the Original Constitution of India?” 1,385, both below the usual, while the film is still all over the news on its box office. Probable cause: two weeks after release the scene questions are answered. Test: none; no more film-answer Shorts.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-17, the Indonesia launch day. Long-form is a Home-feed channel: 169,831 long-form views over 28 days came from the bucket that holds Home and the subscriptions feed, against 4,888 from search. Engaged views were 40.5% of long-form views over 90 days, so a view counts for less than it did before August.
- Most new subscribers click on the channel page, not under a video: 915 subscribers gained over 28 days carried no video, against 545 net from all uploads. Community posts brought 2 on 381,826 views; they buy views, not subscribers.
- The Indonesia long-form reaches the country it is about: a Muslim from Java who grew up with the Ramayana, an Indonesian correcting it, and Indian viewers saying they subscribed.
- Shorts views rose 118.5% week over week on the film Shorts, yet over 28 days Shorts brought 137 upload net subscribers against long-form's 408.
- WhatsApp is the outside source that sends viewers: 12,523 views over the 365-day window against Instagram's 454. The most forwarded videos are the temple tax and Goa long-forms.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form holds most of the week's comments: people from Indonesia and Malaysia adding to it and correcting it, Indian viewers angry at the rewrite, and viewers from other Ramayana countries claiming the story. Under the Sai Pallavi Short the row still draws comments.
- **Indonesians answering back** (positive): "I am a Muslim living in Java, Indonesia, and I have been familiar with the Ramayana and Mahabharata since childhood."
- **A correction from Indonesia** (mixed): "Rama were never worshiped in Classical Nusantara (present day countries describe as malay archipelago) esp. in the Majapahit era"
- **Anger at the rewrite** (negative): "Distortion of our scriptures"
- **Other Ramayana countries claiming the story** (positive): "I'm a Burmese and Buddhist from my home country Myanmar but still big fan of Ramayana"
- **The Sai Pallavi row, still going** (negative): "The irony of playing Sita and defending Ravana in return"
- **Doubters** (negative): "All are mythology, Ram Didn't even exist historically"

Requested topics
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Rajendra Chola's fleet to Srivijaya, the most-liked objection under the Asia long-form
- Bagan in Myanmar
- Hindi versions of the long-forms

## Competitors
The watchlist is still mostly reacting to the Ramayana film. One opening is worth borrowing for the Tipu Short this week, and one title is evidence for the Bali long-form.
- **Hindu Lifestyle**: "Diwali is South Asian... wait.. what?"
  Why it worked: 160,547 views at 31.4x the channel's median, a Short. It opens by stating the claim it is about to knock down (“Diwali is not a Hindu festival. It's a South Asian festival.”) and reacts in the next word (“What?”).
  Steal: Open the Tipu Short the same way: the British verdict on him first, then who wrote it and what they took. Itiha's two Shorts that open like this sit well above the usual, a small sample.
- **The Sham Sharma Show**: "Bali Death Dark Truth"
  Why it worked: 581,330 views at 3.8x the channel's median. There is no transcript in the data, so only the title can be read: the island's name and a promise of something hidden.
  Steal: Evidence that “Bali” carries a title on Indian YouTube. Put the word first in the follow-up's title.

Gaps
- Why Japan backed India's freedom fight: The Emissary's Short (569,338 views) has no match in Itiha's catalogue, and the Rash Behari Bose long-form draft, third version on disk, covers the same alliance.
- Aurangzeb as a long-form: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of Aurangzeb” stands unanswered by every tracked channel and by Itiha (see ideas).

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan, 20 November: due today, no script  
  Signal: The calendar's date for him is today, and a Tipu Jayanti row is in News18 Marathi on 19 November. The radar's step is to publish on the date, titled with the searched name “tipu sultan history”. (Moments radar, owner's note, news)  
  Make: Decision 1: script and record today, publish by 22 November, judge on day three. If only one Short can be made before 24 November, make Tegh Bahadur and drop this one on the Today tab.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November  
  Signal: The top-ranked dated moment, four days out. The radar's step this week is to record and cut the Short, titled with the searched name “guru tegh bahadur history”. The calendar flags the martyrdom framing as one to avoid. (Moments radar, calendar)  
  Make: Decision 2: script by 21 November, record on 22, publish the evening of 23 November, judge on 26 November.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: The Malay Ramayana Short, written 19 November  
  Signal: The Indonesia long-form runs at 875.5 views an hour. The Short on disk retells its strangest scene, Ravana's power granted by Allah, and hands off to it in the last line. (Script on disk, own long-form)  
  Make: Record it this week and publish it between the two dated Shorts, with the long-form as its related video. That it sends viewers to the long-form is a guess.
- **watch, skip, 2/5**: Birsa Munda on Wikipedia  
  Signal: Hindi readership at 8x its 30-day median and English at 5.32x, five days after his birth anniversary, with a new song and a Parliament tribute in the news. (Wikipedia pageviews, news)  
  Make: Skip this week: two dated Shorts are already due, and freedom-fighter biographies have done below the usual here. If it is made later, the angle is the mission school he walked out of before he rose against the British, not his death.
- **watch, short, 3/5**: 4 December 1829, the sati ban: a script is already on disk  
  Signal: The radar has Bentinck's regulation in 14 days. The wife-selling Short, written 17 September and never recorded, is built on that date: the year Britain banned sati, Englishmen were selling their wives at market. (Moments radar, script on disk)  
  Make: Clear its three VERIFY flags, record by 3 December and publish on 4 December. It rests on the date: the one sati Short so far, “How Missionaries Turned Sati Into a Fundraiser”, has 1,768 views.
- **watch, skip, 1/5**: Two films on 4 December: Eetha and Maatrubhumi  
  Signal: Eetha is a biopic with Shraddha Kapoor and Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace a war film with Salman Khan, both released 4 December. The data does not say who or what either film is about. (Moments radar)  
  Make: Nothing until it is known who each film is about. Check by 27 November, when the radar's next step is due; if either is about a figure in the channel's lane, the plan is a Short between release day +1 and +9, judged on day three.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [3/5, long] **Why Bali Is Still Hindu: The Priests Who Left Java**  
  Identity and religion stakes: the one island in Indonesia that stayed Hindu; Empire mechanism: the sultanates that ended Majapahit; Hidden history: the other half of the Indonesia story  
  source: Decision 3. A guess from the Indonesia long-form's comments; its launch-day subscriber rate supports keeping it.
- [3/5, long] **What Aurangzeb's Own Court Wrote Down**  
  Villain plus hypocrisy: his official chronicle, Maasir-i-Alamgiri, records the orders in his own court's words; Identity and religion stakes: the temples at Kashi and Mathura; Contested history: the claim that the Mughals did not destroy temples, which the channel's Irfan Habib Shorts already took on  
  source: Open in the counter-channel list: Mohak Mangal's “Reality of Aurangzeb” has no answer from any tracked channel or Itiha. The channel's two largest videos are Aurangzeb Shorts, but in a film window; the Tegh Bahadur Short is the first test without one.
- [3/5, long] **How Robert Clive Took Bengal's Treasury Home**  
  Empire or extraction mechanism: the payments after Plassey; Villain plus hypocrisy: Parliament heard him and let him keep it; Decolonisation reframe: the founder of British India as a looter on his own record  
  source: Calendar: Clive died on 22 November 1774. The shape is the channel's best converter, a villain convicted by a payment he could not deny. Rests on that lane, not on a test of Clive.
- [2/5, short] **Why Thailand's Kings Are Named Rama**  
  Identity stakes: a Hindu epic at the head of a Buddhist kingdom; Hidden history: how the name reached the throne  
  source: On disk since 19 November, waiting for the owner's edit. Made for the Asia long-form's viewers, where a comment lists the titles Thai kings took. Rests on that audience, not on a result.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,533 followers, up 273 in 7 days, 39 a day. Today's reel on Sonia Gandhi's book is too new to read. Carousels remain the growth format at 3.76x the median reach of reels.

Do more
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 36 followers (89 posts); outside the band, 12 (15 posts). Pooled rate 2.97 vs 1.88 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 399 followers a month at stake.
- Write carousels in the revision lane  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 22 for the other lanes (39 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 12.5k, conversion 3.77 vs 2.12 per 1k. 383 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  19 of 102 rated posts are shared above the median (25.4/1k) but convert below it (2.2/1k): median 12.8k reach for a median 12 followers. The 32 posts that do both average 290 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 1,005 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 83.5k reach between them and 118 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 94 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **now**: If not done yet, answer the Indonesian comments under “Why Ravana Gets His Powers From ALLAH in This Ramayana” in one pinned reply: where the Adam-and-Allah version comes from, and what Majapahit worshipped. /replies drafts it.  
  The video is still climbing, so every new viewer reads its top comments, and two of the most-liked are from Java and Indonesia. That a reply helps is a guess.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, put the Indonesia long-form on the end screen and pinned comment of “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”, and make it the channel page's video for visitors who have not subscribed.  
  The Asia long-form has 158,693 views on the same subject, and 915 subscribers over 28 days came from the channel page rather than any video. That either move helps is a guess.
- **this_week**: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 0 views since 3 November, and the two Shorts published with it, “Itihasa vs Myth” (82) and “Is Caste Unique to India?” (255).  
  A public Short gets at least a handful of views, so none at all points to its visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
- **later**: Add the Google Analytics property number to the settings file.  
  Without it the brief cannot say how itiha.info is doing. Search Console shows the site found on Google almost only for its own name.
